title: 2026 Pan-African Digital Payment Adoption
objective: Establish how businesses and households across six African markets actually use digital payment rails, which interoperability failures cost them money, and what would make them move a larger share of volume onto cross-border instruments.
audience: Finance leads, treasury managers and owners of businesses transacting in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda, Egypt and South Africa, plus households that send or receive cross-border payments.
consentNotice: Your responses are anonymous and will be reported only in aggregate. No payment account details, card numbers or personally identifying information are requested or should be entered. Participation is voluntary and you may stop at any point without giving a reason.
incentive: Participants may request the summary findings report on completion.

questions.prompt: Which market do you primarily transact in?
questions.helpText: Select the market where the majority of your transaction volume occurs.

questions.prompt: Which of these payment instruments does your organisation use at least monthly?
Roughly what share of your monthly transaction volume is cross-border?
How long does a typical cross-border payment take to settle for you?
options: It varies too much to state

logic.description: Shown only to respondents who reported cross-border volume in question 3.

questions.prompt: Rate the reliability of the payment rails you depend on most.
questions.helpText: Statement: 'The payment rails I depend on most settle when the provider says they will.'

questions.prompt: On a scale of 1 to 10, how much does payment failure or delay cost your organisation each month?
What single change would move the most volume onto a cross-border digital instrument?
questions.helpText: One sentence is enough. Please do not include account numbers or personal details.

buckets.label: It varies too much to state

title: Remote Executive Work Practices & Board Engagement
objective: Understand how executive teams and boards have adapted their meeting practice to hybrid and remote working, and whether the change has affected the quality of scrutiny, dissent and decision records.
audience: Board members, company secretaries, executives and senior governance professionals at organisations with a hybrid or fully remote meeting practice.
consentNotice: Responses are anonymous. Please do not name your organisation, colleagues or any identifiable matter under discussion. Aggregate results only will be published.

questions.prompt: What is your primary role in relation to the board?
How are board meetings currently held?
options: Predominantly in person with remote option

questions.prompt: Which practices has your board adopted since moving to hybrid working?
options: Shorter meetings with more frequent sessions
Written dissent recorded in the minutes

questions.prompt: Has the willingness of non-executives to challenge management changed?
On a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you that your minutes accurately record the substance of discussion?
What has been lost in the move away from fully in-person meetings?
questions.helpText: A short paragraph is welcome. Do not include names or identifiable matters.

buckets.label: Predominantly in person with remote option
Shorter meetings with more frequent sessions
Written dissent recorded in the minutes

title: Consumer Sentiments on Sustainable Packaging in Fast-Moving Goods
objective: Test whether stated willingness to pay for sustainable packaging survives contact with a realistic price differential, and identify which packaging claims consumers actually trust.
audience: Adult consumers who purchase fast-moving consumer goods at least weekly, across the United Kingdom, Ireland and three continental European markets.
consentNotice: Your responses will be used for aggregated market research reporting only. No personal data is sold or shared with third parties. You may withdraw by contacting the research desk before the closing date.
moderationNote: Awaiting editorial review: question 6 asks respondents to estimate a household income band, which the moderation desk has flagged as sensitive. Recommend making it optional and adding an explicit 'prefer not to say' option before approval.

questions.prompt: How often do you check packaging material or disposal instructions before buying a product?
Which packaging claims do you trust?
options: A recycling instruction with a local authority reference

questions.prompt: You are choosing between two equivalent products. The more sustainably packaged option costs 15% more. What do you do?
For which categories would you pay the 15% premium?

logic.description: Shown only to respondents who said the premium depends on category in question 3.

questions.prompt: 'I would change brand over packaging alone.'
Which household income band does your purchase fall into?
questions.helpText: Optional. Used only for aggregate segmentation.

title: Small Business Adoption of Automated Bookkeeping Tools
objective: Measure how small and micro businesses adopt automated bookkeeping, what stops adoption, and whether adoption has changed the relationship between the owner and their accountant.
audience: Owners, finance managers and accountants serving businesses with fewer than fifty employees.
consentNotice: Responses may be attributed to your organisation in aggregate sector reporting. Individual answers will not be published or sold. Contact the research desk to withdraw.

questions.prompt: How many people does your organisation employ?
How are your books currently maintained?
options: Accounting software maintained by an external accountant
Fully outsourced to an accountant or bookkeeper

questions.prompt: Which of these have you automated in the last twelve months?
options: VAT or sales tax return preparation

questions.prompt: What was the main barrier to automating further?
options: No barrier — we are fully automated

logic.description: Hidden for organisations still on paper records, who are routed to question 5.

questions.prompt: On a scale of 1 to 10, how much has automation changed the frequency of your conversations with your accountant?
Describe one task you still do manually that you would automate if you could.

title: Secondary School Digital Learning Access in Urban Households
objective: Document the practical barriers to digital learning in urban secondary school households: device availability, connectivity quality, shared access and the effect on homework completion.
audience: Parents and carers of secondary school pupils, and teaching staff working in urban secondary schools.
consentNotice: This survey does not collect information about any identifiable child. Please do not include pupil names, school names or any detail that could identify a specific pupil or household.

questions.prompt: Are you responding as a parent or carer, or as teaching staff?
How many devices suitable for schoolwork are available in the household?

logic.description: Household questions are shown only to parents and carers.

questions.prompt: How often does a pupil have to wait for access to a shared device to complete work?

logic.description: Shown where at least one device is available.

questions.prompt: 'Home connectivity is reliable enough for video lessons and submission deadlines.'
On a scale of 1 to 10, how much does device access affect homework completion in your experience?
What single support would most improve the situation?

title: Patient Experience of Remote GP Consultations
objective: Assess patient experience of remote primary care consultations across access, continuity, privacy and the willingness to raise a sensitive concern remotely.
audience: Adults who have had at least one remote consultation with a general practice in the last twenty-four months.
consentNotice: This survey asks about your experience of healthcare, not about your clinical condition. Do not include your name, NHS or patient number, medication details or the name of your practice. Responses are anonymous and reported in aggregate only. This survey is not a route to clinical advice or urgent care.

questions.prompt: Which format was your most recent remote consultation?
options: Online form with a clinician response

questions.prompt: How long did you wait between requesting and receiving the consultation?
Were you in a private place where you could speak freely?
Would you raise a sensitive health concern in a remote consultation?
questions.helpText: Statement: 'I would raise a sensitive health concern remotely as readily as in person.'

questions.prompt: Did you see the same clinician as in a previous consultation?

logic.description: Continuity question shown to all respondents who completed the access questions.

questions.prompt: On a scale of 1 to 10, how confident were you in the clinician's assessment without a physical examination?
What would make a remote consultation work better for you?

buckets.label: Online form with a clinician response

title: Public Attitudes to Urban Congestion Charging
objective: Measure public attitudes to road user charging in cities, including the conditions under which respondents say they would support a scheme and the distributional concerns they raise.
audience: Adults living or working in urban areas with a population above 250,000.
consentNotice: Responses are anonymous and reported in aggregate. Political affiliation is not collected. Do not include any personal or identifying information.

questions.prompt: How do you usually travel to work or your main daily activity?
Would you support a congestion charge in your city?
Under which conditions would you support a scheme?
options: Exemptions for disabled users and essential workers
A daily cap on total charges
Improved alternatives before the charge starts
A public vote on the scheme
No conditions would make me support it

logic.description: Condition questions are hidden from respondents who answered 'No' in question 2.

questions.prompt: 'A congestion charge falls disproportionately on people with the least choice.'
On a scale of 1 to 10, how much do you trust your city authority to spend the revenue as promised?
What would change your mind about road user charging?

buckets.label: Exemptions for disabled users and essential workers

title: Founder Access to Early-Stage Capital Outside Major Hubs
objective: Test whether geography still determines access to early-stage capital, and identify which non-equity instruments founders outside major hubs actually use to reach their first revenue milestones.
audience: Founders and early employees of companies under five years old with fewer than twenty-five staff, based outside London, Paris, Berlin, New York and San Francisco.
consentNotice: Company-level responses may be used in aggregate regional reporting. Individual financial terms, investor names and non-public valuations will not be published. You may request a copy of the aggregate findings on completion.

questions.prompt: How old is your company?
Which sources have you actually drawn capital from?
How many investor meetings did you hold before your last successful raise?
How much did travel to investor meetings cost you, in time and money?
'Being outside a major hub has materially slowed my access to capital.'
On a scale of 1 to 10, how well does the available non-equity finance match your needs?
What one change to the regional finance landscape would help most?

title: Enterprise Buyer Expectations of B2B Software Onboarding
objective: Establish what enterprise buyers expect during the first ninety days after purchase, which onboarding failures most often trigger a non-renewal conversation, and what evidence buyers want to see before renewal.
audience: Procurement leads, IT buyers and operational sponsors who have signed or managed a business software purchase above £25,000 annual contract value.
consentNotice: Responses are used for aggregate product research. Do not disclose confidential contract terms, vendor names under non-disclosure, or any information you are not authorised to share.

questions.prompt: What was the annual contract value of your most recent software purchase?
Which of these did the vendor deliver in the first ninety days?
options: A written success plan with dates
Integration with at least one existing system

questions.prompt: How long did it take to reach the first measurable business outcome?
What triggered a non-renewal conversation at your organisation?
'The vendor's onboarding matched what was promised in the sales process.'
On a scale of 1 to 10, how much evidence of value did you have before the renewal decision?
What would you require in an onboarding plan that vendors rarely offer?

buckets.label: A written success plan with dates
Integration with at least one existing system

title: Cloud Migration Cost Predictability in Mid-Market Firms
objective: Quantify the gap between forecast and actual infrastructure cost after migration among mid-market firms, and identify which governance practices correlate with a smaller gap.
audience: Technology leaders, finance business partners and operations directors at organisations with 50–1,000 employees that completed a major infrastructure migration in the last three years.
consentNotice: Responses are anonymous. Do not disclose your employer's contract terms, vendor pricing or any information subject to a non-disclosure agreement. Aggregate reporting only.

questions.prompt: When did your organisation complete its most significant infrastructure migration?
How did actual monthly infrastructure cost compare with the pre-migration forecast in the first year?
options: We did not produce a forecast

questions.prompt: Which cost governance practices were in place by month six?
options: Budget alerts with a named owner
Monthly cost review with finance present

questions.prompt: Who owns the infrastructure budget after migration?
'We can explain a month-on-month cost movement within five working days.'
On a scale of 1 to 10, how much of your post-migration cost was avoidable waste?
What would you do differently, in one sentence?
